$description: Type, weight, size, rhythm and motion primitives. Three families with three distinct jobs — display carries the voice, sans does the work, mono aligns the digits. Every family declares a real fallback stack, because a webfont that fails to load must degrade to something with similar metrics rather than to Times.

display.$description: Headings and display type only. A didone: hairline-to-stem contrast is extreme, which is precisely where the elegance lives — and at its heavy weights that same contrast reads as bold rather than delicate. Never set below 20px; the hairlines vanish and it turns to mush at UI sizes.

sans.$description: Every interface surface — labels, body, buttons, help text. Chosen over the obvious geometric options because it holds up at 12px in dense tables, which a Futura-lineage face does not. Warm enough to sit with the sand neutral without fighting it.

mono.$description: Token names, hex values, code, and any column of digits. Deliberately DM Mono rather than an unrelated mono: it shares DM Sans's skeleton and metrics, so a code snippet beside body text reads as the same voice at a different pitch instead of as a foreign object.

bold.$description: Display face only. DM Sans at 700 in UI reads as shouting; the hierarchy is carried by size and colour instead.

display.$description: The floor for the display face. Below this a didone's hairlines drop out.
Display type sets tighter — large didone caps leave too much optical space at 1.25.
Large type needs negative tracking; the default spacing is designed for text sizes.

label.$description: Uppercase micro-labels only. Caps set at default tracking read as cramped.
